findings.title: adport REST/MCP write surfaces apply with no enforced human approver
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/tools/write.ts:40-66 (same guardedWriteTool handler: with pending_operation_id goes straight to ctx.engine.apply, no actor/human check)
platform/apps/cloud/app/mcp/route.ts:40-63 + platform/packages/mcp/src/index.ts:122 (write tools registered for tools:write principals)
findings.description: The two-step adport write gate (validate then apply) is not a human approval. Any holder of a tools:write key, over REST /api/v1/tools/{tool} or the MCP /mcp connector, can call validate then apply in two calls with no second human. The dashboard apply route DOES enforce role + non-self-approval, but the REST/MCP surfaces do not. This breaks the product-level 'AI proposes -> human approves -> apply' invariant and contradicts README.md:79. The engine/Assistant path remains fail-closed and proposal-only; this hole is adport-native, plan-gated, off the Assistant path, but shipped.
findings.recommendation: Enforce an out-of-band approver on EVERY apply surface, not just the dashboard. Route high-risk operations to mandatory human apply. This is the single most important safety fix and gates any live enablement.

findings.title: Generic *_api_update / *_api_remove allow uncapped status/bid/targeting/destructive mutations
evidence: platform/packages/google/src/provider.ts:310-339 (planApiCreate DOES coerce campaign status to PAUSED and budget-checks creates - the create path is partially mitigated)
findings.description: The generic API-shaped tools let a tools:write principal mutate non-budget fields with budget-only policy. A status flip to ENABLED via google_api_update starts delivery; bid and targeting changes pass; google_api_remove is destructive and uncapped - with no risk flag and no human on the REST/MCP path (combines with K2-P1-01). Correction to C7-02/C14-P1-02: api_create of a campaign IS coerced to PAUSED and budget creates ARE policy-checked, so the genuine uncapped autonomous-mutation surface is UPDATE (status/bid/targeting) and REMOVE, not create.
findings.recommendation: Retire or default-gate the generic *_api_* tools from the tenant/agent runtime; mirror the engine's classify_risk on the adport write path; cap/flag non-budget mutations (status, destructive) and require human apply for them.

findings.title: Model receives zero tenant/business/locale context and only analyses fixture accounts
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:139-171,383-392 (host refuses live credentials and pins paid_media_data_mode=sample in both demo and live)

findings.title: No prompt caching; unbounded context growth
evidence: engine/.venv/.../middleware/summarization.py:274-286 (compaction only at ~850k tokens with the main model as summarizer)
findings.description: The ~5.6k-token stable prefix and the whole transcript are re-billed every call; no ephemeral cache_control is ever set, and compaction fires only at ~850k tokens using the main model as summarizer. Caching is the single biggest cost lever and the prefix is already cache-friendly.
findings.recommendation: Set ephemeral cache breakpoints on the stable system+tools prefix and the last message; use a Haiku-class summarizer distinct from the main model; target >=70% cached input on turn >=2.

findings.title: Model failures masked as HTTP-200 prose; all errors retried; no run deadline; client abort orphans the run
evidence: engine/.venv/.../langchain/agents/middleware/model_retry.py:192-195 (returns AIMessage 'Model call failed after N attempts...')
findings.description: A model outage is returned to the user as a normal HTTP-200 assistant sentence rather than a typed error; deterministic/config errors are retried as if transient; there is no per-run/per-request wall-clock deadline; a client abort at 240s does not cancel the engine run, which keeps spending.
findings.recommendation: Surface typed, localized errors to the UI; restrict retries to transient classes (429/5xx/timeout) with jittered backoff; add an asyncio.wait_for run deadline; cancel the engine run on client disconnect.

findings.title: No per-thread concurrency control/idempotency on chat; non-atomic live apply
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:87-125 (apply is get->applyWrite->delete, no FOR UPDATE/transaction, no idempotency key)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:397,413-418 (get filters consumed_at is null; delete is unconditional update set consumed_at=now())
findings.description: Concurrent or duplicate applies can both pass the pending-operation get before either deletes, executing a live mutation twice; the apply path takes no idempotency key into applyWrite and holds no lock/transaction. Chat turns have no per-thread serialization.
findings.recommendation: Make apply an atomic consume (... where consumed_at is null returning *) with an idempotency key passed into applyWrite; add a per-thread lock + idempotency key on the chat path.

findings.title: Account scoping checks one argument; engine trusts provider readOnlyHint for read/write classification
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/catalog.py:162-188 (classification reads annotations.readOnlyHint straight from the Pipeboard MCP metadata)
findings.description: The cloud account-scope authorizer only inspects top-level account_id/customer_id; other id-bearing args (ad_account_id, login_customer_id, single-resource ids, list args) pass unscoped under the shared token. Separately, the engine classifies a Pipeboard tool as a model-callable READ purely on its provider-supplied readOnlyHint; a mutating tool named to evade the deny patterns (e.g. campaign_update) and flagged readOnlyHint=true would be invoked as an ungoverned 'read'.
findings.recommendation: Scope every id-bearing argument; maintain an explicit host-side read-tool allowlist (names) so readOnlyHint is corroborated not trusted; alarm when a catalog refresh flips a tool's class/hint.

findings.title: Dashboard self-approval guard bypassed for API-key-created pending ops

Provenance of who requested the change is also lost.
findings.recommendation: Record the API-key owner as created_by; treat a null requester as fail-closed (require an explicit distinct approver) rather than skipping the check.

findings.title: Model filesystem write covers artifacts/reports/kill-switch; integrity is SHA-256 not HMAC
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/runtime/local.py:47-49 (/workspace/** write-allowed, includes artifact store, report out, kill-switch path)
engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/artifacts.py:134-145 (integrity is a plain SHA-256 next to the payload, not an HMAC)
findings.description: The model's filesystem write permission covers all of /workspace/** including the artifact store, report output directory, and the kill-switch path, and artifact integrity is a plain SHA-256 adjacent to the payload rather than a keyed HMAC, so a model-written artifact can be self-consistent.
findings.recommendation: Narrow model write scope away from artifact/report/kill-switch paths; use a keyed HMAC for artifact integrity.

findings.title: Budget cap re-check skipped at apply; expired outcome never written
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:110-153 (apply calls checkStaticPolicy only; checkBudgetPolicy defined but not invoked at apply)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:420-425 (markPendingOutcome/sweep exists but is never invoked; expired never written)
findings.description: A budget cap tightened between validate and apply is not enforced because apply re-runs only checkStaticPolicy (protected accounts), not checkBudgetPolicy. The expired proposal outcome is declared but never written because no sweep job runs.
findings.recommendation: Re-check budget policy at apply, not only validate; schedule the existing pending sweep to write expired outcomes.

findings.title: Engine-side outcome memory systematically wrong (every bridged proposal recorded as rejected)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/bridge.ts:94,99 (records adport status pending, then handoff calls rejectOnEngine)
engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/writes.py:498-511 (engine marks the proposal rejected on the reject endpoint)
findings.description: When adport takes over a bridged engine proposal it calls the engine's reject endpoint as a hand-off, so the engine's own outcome memory records every bridged proposal as rejected regardless of what actually happened; the true outcome (applied/rejected/expired) lives only in adport and is never fed back. This corrupts any future learning signal drawn from engine state.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a distinct handed_off decision instead of reject, and write the adport outcome back into the thread as a system message.

findings.title: No durable tenant/account/long-term/outcome memory or learning loop
findings.description: There is no store, no per-org/account/long-term memory, and no outcome loop: measurement_plan and reversal_plan are parsed and discarded, nothing schedules a measurement or records whether an executed change worked. This is what makes the system a dashboard-with-chat rather than a media buyer that learns.
findings.recommendation: Add a markting_decision_outcomes table seeded from markting_engine_proposals + measurement_plan; invoke the existing pending sweep to measure at maturation; learn only from confirmed facts, measured outcomes, and accept/reject rates (never to change limits/approvers/protected lists).

K2.summary: The AI layer is a dashboard-with-chat over synthetic data, not an intelligent operating system - CONFIRMED from code at HEAD 2e68a7f. What is REAL: a genuinely fail-closed proposal engine (ProposalOnlyWriteProvider, empty approver set, fail-closed WriteGate kill switch checked even for fakes, signed single-use claims, reconciling readback), a deny-by-default engine tool catalog, a structurally strong model-output->adport boundary (fixed allowlist + alias map + schema, test-verified), and a code-owned deterministic numeric/report layer. What is SCRIPTED/MOCK: the default demo mode is a regex choosing one of two canned scripts whose 'recommendation' is always g-103->240, and ALL data is three USD fixtures in both demo and live mode because the host pins sample mode and refuses any live credential - no tenant account ever reaches the model, which receives only {text}. What is STRUCTURALLY MISSING: per-turn tenant/business/locale context, durable memory/learning/outcome loop, Arabic reasoning/reports, creative/frequency/change-history tools and significance/decomposition signals, metering/quota/caching, tracing/token capture, per-org isolation of workspace/report-index/history, and universal human approval on writes. Invariant ruling (CONFIRMED, every bypass re-verified): 'AI may only propose' HOLDS on the engine/Assistant path (attempts 1-6 blocked, VERIFIED_CODE/TEST) but is BROKEN on adport's autonomous REST/MCP write surfaces - any tools:write holder can validate then apply with no second human (attempts 7-8, P1), generic *_api_update/remove make uncapped status/bid/targeting/destructive changes (attempt 9, P1, with a create-path correction to C7-02: api_create of a campaign is coerced PAUSED and budget-checked), plus SoD gaps on the human path (10-12). 15/15 primary spot-checks HELD, one PARTIAL (the generic-create blast radius is narrower than C7-02 framed - the real hole is update/remove). Top gaps in order: (1) no live data to the model, (2) no human approval on REST/MCP writes, (3) uncapped generic api mutations, (4) cross-tenant state holes (P1 now, P0 on live), (5) zero tenant context, (6) no outcome loop/learning, (7) deletion/retention miss engine memory, (8) no metering/caching, (9) no observability, (10) Arabic/regional doctrine absent. Target architecture ratified as five governed layers in a safety-first sequence: AI Gateway (ship Option A safety items unconditionally, self-hosted Option B at multi-tenant live), tenant-scoped Intelligence Layer delivered via a new engine context field, Marketing Memory in adport Postgres with human-confirmed facts and no learned value changing a limit, a single human-gated/metered/observable Recommendation pipeline with the engine risk classifier mirrored on the adport write path and the generic api tools retired, and an outcome loop using the dormant pending sweep. Confidence 0.86; live-model behaviour, Docker contents, DB concurrency, the MDA path and dollar figures remain NOT_VERIFIED by construction.

K3.summary: I validated 04-system-architecture-map.md against the code by walking every Mermaid diagram edge-by-edge: 27 spot-checks, 26 HELD, 1 PARTIAL (the 'SandboxProvider near-line-for-line copy of SyntheticProvider' wording overstates it — 211 vs 130 lines, a parallel implementation not a verbatim copy), 0 FAILED. The map is structurally accurate and I endorse it as the authoritative architecture document, with one material amendment: its section 12 positive finding that the single-write-path invariant is 'structurally present and fail-closed' is true for the engine/bridge/Assistant path but overstated for adport's own REST /api/v1/tools/[tool] and MCP /mcp surfaces, which apply a previewed write on the second call with scope enforcement only and no enforced human approver (the requester!=approver check exists only in the dashboard apply route). I resolve this in favour of K2/C13/C14/J2: the invariant is conditional (K3-03, P1). I vouch for the map's two P1s: C1 non-atomic/double apply (the apply seam has no atomic claim and does three non-transactional writes across two systems; the correct pattern exists upstream in pma_approvals but not in adport) and C2 (the engine is fixture-only in every mode yet proposals can route to real accounts via alias binding). Architecture verdicts: the engine is an unscalable SPOF (one process, one :adport-bridge caller for all tenants, per-process scripted-model state, one global asyncio.Lock, single-file report index) and must stay single-replica/fixture-only until externalised; chat is a minutes-long synchronous call with no queue/idempotency/cancellation; the two-Postgres split-brain plus destructive supabase db reset on every make up is a real data-consistency/migration hazard; the engine host's binding to ~10 private/test-only upstream symbols with no drift check and no root CI is tight accidental coupling. Phase 0 decisions everything depends on: (1) make apply atomic+transactional before any live write; (2) enforce requester!=approver on ALL write surfaces incl REST/MCP; (3) decide the engine multi-tenant model (per-tenant identity, per-thread serialisation, externalised state) before a 2nd replica or live mode; (4) resolve the two-DB split-brain and add forward-only migrations for both; (5) stand up root CI + upstream-edit drift check; (6) keep fixture-only fail-closed default and gate alias-to-real-account binding; (7) introduce the missing event/outbox backbone. Memo at docs/audit/agents/K3.md. P1=3, P2=6, P3=1, GAP=1. Confidence 0.86; the residual gap is entirely the un-runnable envelope (container builds, live mode, production Supabase config).

findings.title: Pending-operation apply is not atomic -> concurrent double-apply to ad platforms (invariant 12 BROKEN)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:383-411 (PostgresPendingStore.get is plain select ... where consumed_at is null, no for update)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:413-418 (delete is update ... set consumed_at=now() where id/organization_id, NO 'and consumed_at is null' compare-and-set)
contrast platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:76-104 (OAuth consume uses db().begin + for update + consumedAt check)
findings.description: Two near-simultaneous POST /api/approvals/{id}/apply (double-click, retry, two admins) both pass the unlocked get (both see consumed_at null), both call provider.applyWrite, then both set consumed_at. Nothing serializes read-check-consume, so a real platform write executes twice (budget applied twice, campaign created twice). Only sequential replay is tested. The sibling OAuth consume shows the correct pattern was known and not applied here.
findings.recommendation: Make consume compare-and-set: update ... set consumed_at=now() where id=... and consumed_at is null returning id, run it (with select ... for update) inside db().begin BEFORE applyWrite, treat 0 rows as already-consumed; add a concurrency test; forward idempotency keys to each provider mutation.

findings.title: Stripe subscription events applied with no ordering/version guard (stale state re-grants entitlements)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/billing.ts:119-140 (processStripeEvent dispatches on event.type, dedups by event_id only)
findings.description: Stripe does not guarantee webhook delivery order. The handler overwrites organization_subscriptions from whatever event.data.object contains and re-runs plan-based account enablement without comparing event.created or a per-subscription version. An out-of-order customer.subscription.updated(active) delivered after customer.subscription.deleted(canceled) reactivates the org to a paid plan and re-enables ad accounts. Active plan governs maxActiveAccounts, i.e. how many accounts may spend. Reachable in normal operation.
findings.recommendation: Re-fetch the authoritative subscription via stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(id) before writing, or persist and compare event.created plus a per-subscription high-water mark and drop stale writes; add a regression test delivering two out-of-order updates.

findings.title: Production Next.js 16.3.1 ships with 3 critical RCE advisories
evidence: E9 pnpm audit --prod exit 1: GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 (AVIF image-optimization RCE) and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (next/og ImageResponse RCE), both platform-independent; patched >=16.3.6
findings.description: The internet-facing cloud app is pinned to a Next.js release with three known critical RCE CVEs; the AVIF image-optimization and next/og RCEs are platform-independent and apply if those features are reachable. I carry E9's VERIFIED_RUNTIME (audit executed) since I had no network to re-run it.
findings.recommendation: Bump next >=16.3.6, regenerate pnpm-lock.yaml, add to a release gate. Escalates to P0 if image-optimization/next/og is reachable from any route (NOT_VERIFIED - out of my code-read scope).

findings.title: No supply-chain / secret / CI gate runs on the shipped repo
evidence: workflows exist only under platform/.github/workflows and engine/.github/workflows, which GitHub discovers only from repo root
both dependabot.yml target directory '/' relative to their own subtree
findings.description: The monorepo vendors the two upstream projects as plain directories. GitHub Actions, Dependabot and the engine Gitleaks job are discovered only from <repo-root>/.github, which is empty, so none of the vendored workflows run on the actual shipped repo: no build/test gate, no dependency scan, no secret scan. Nothing would have surfaced SEC-04 or any future vulnerable dep/leaked secret.
findings.recommendation: Add a root .github/workflows invoking platform and engine jobs with correct working-directory/path filters and a root dependabot.yml; confirm what actually runs on the hosting repo. INFERRED on non-execution because the hosting repo might add a root .github not in this checkout.

findings.title: No owner/admin revocation of MCP OAuth grants; grants survive member deprovisioning
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/mcp-oauth-repository.ts:263-298 (authenticateMcpOAuthAccessToken checks jti/revoked/expiry/claims but never joins organization_memberships)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/tenant-admin.ts:117-146 (removeOrganizationMember deletes membership + writes audit, never revokes mcp_oauth_* tokens)
platform/apps/cloud/app/oauth/revoke/route.ts:15 (only revoke path requires the client's own token+clientId)
findings.description: Merge of E2-01 (P1, no admin revoke) and E1-02 (P2, survives deprovisioning). Token auth never re-checks membership and member removal never revokes the member's MCP tokens; the only revoke path is the RFC 7009 token-holder path. A deprovisioned member's access token (1h) and refresh token (30d) keep authenticating and minting fresh access against the org for up to 30 days, against an agent that can spend ad budget, with no tenant-side kill switch.
findings.recommendation: Add an authenticated owner/admin 'disconnect this app' endpoint that revokes all access+refresh tokens for a grant; revoke a user's mcp_oauth_* tokens inside removeOrganizationMember/changeOrganizationMemberRole; join organization_memberships in token auth.

findings.title: Four-eyes separation-of-duties control is bypassable three ways (self-approval)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/approvals/[id]/apply/route.ts:22 (guard short-circuits when row.createdBy is null; API-key/engine pendings have created_by null)

platform/apps/cloud/app/api/v1/tools/[tool]/route.ts:5-13 + platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:104 (REST/MCP apply routes through PolicyEngine which checks provider+hash only, never actor; apiPrincipal has no userId)
findings.description: Upgraded from E10-06's P3. The advertised 'Requester != approver' control holds only in the narrow dashboard-created + dashboard-applied + non-null-createdBy + env-off path. It is skipped for every API-key/engine-created pending (null created_by), absent entirely on the REST/MCP apply path (PolicyEngine has no actor check), and off by default in the shipped demo env. It governs real ad-spend writes and is materially weaker than documented.
findings.recommendation: Record created_by_api_key_id/applied_by on pending rows; move the self-approval rule into the PolicyEngine/pending store so REST/MCP applies are covered; ship MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=false in all templates. Stays P2 (below P1) because exploitation requires an already-authorized owner/admin or owner/admin-created tools:write key and is org-scoped.

findings.title: Cloud master secrets injected into the engine container (NEW, from J2-04)
evidence: docker-compose.yml:17,40,47 (both cloud and engine use env_file: .env)
root .env.example holds SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, superuser SUPABASE_DB_URL (postgres:postgres), ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY, ADPORT_API_KEY_PEPPER, ADPORT_MCP_OAUTH_SIGNING_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
findings.description: The engine process (which runs model-driven tool code in live mode) is handed the entire cloud secret set via the shared env file, including the vault key for every tenant's OAuth tokens, the superuser DB DSN, the API-key pepper, the MCP signing key and the Stripe secret - none of which the engine needs. An engine compromise becomes a full cloud compromise. The E-series missed this; J2-04 found it and I confirm it.
findings.recommendation: Give each service its own env file or an explicit compose environment: allowlist; never pass the Supabase service key, superuser DSN, encryption key, pepper or signing key to the engine.

findings.title: Engine exposes unauthenticated /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json, /health, /markting/info (from J2-05)
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:326-336 (/markting/info no auth; returns mode, write-provider class, kill-switch state, approver list, account aliases)
J2 probe: all five returned 200 without a token; /openapi.json enumerates /proposals/{id}/approve and /edit
findings.description: The engine's FastAPI surface exposes interactive docs and an unauthenticated /markting/info that discloses internal configuration. Bounded because the compose port is not published to the host, so this is information disclosure on the compose network only.
findings.recommendation: Build the app with docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None; put /markting/info behind the caller dependency; keep /health minimal (status only).

findings.title: Budget caps not re-checked at apply (invariant 5 PARTIAL)
findings.description: max_budget_delta_pct and max_daily_budget_micros are enforced only against the validate-time preview. Between validate and apply the org policy can be tightened; apply re-checks only protected accounts, so a pending op validated under looser rails applies after rails tighten, up to the TTL (default 15 min). The engine.ts:110 comment 'Policy may have changed ... re-check' overstates what runs.
findings.recommendation: Re-run checkBudgetPolicy in apply() against the current policy (the preview budgetDeltas are stored on the pending row), or re-preview and compare before executing.

findings.title: Completed real write can have no audit record (invariant 13 PARTIAL)
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:113-123 (order is applyWrite -> audit.append('applied') -> pending.delete, no pre-write intent row, no transaction)
findings.description: If audit.append throws after applyWrite succeeds (DB hiccup/outage), the platform write has already happened, the applied audit row is never written, and because delete is never reached the pending stays applicable - enabling a retried second write (compounds SEC-02). Invariant 13 fails under audit-store failure.
findings.recommendation: Write an 'applying' intent audit row before applyWrite, and/or consume the pending in the same transaction as the audit append; reconcile intent vs applied asynchronously and alert on orphans.

findings.title: Engine /proposals/{id}/reject and /edit perform no caller/ownership authorization
findings.description: Any holder of a valid engine bearer can reject or revise any pending proposal by UUID regardless of thread ownership; the read-visibility check is absent on these mutating endpoints. Mitigated in the markting product by the single adport-bridge caller and the bridge FORBIDDEN_PATHS blocking /edit and /approve, so not reachable cross-tenant through the product - but a genuine horizontal-authz gap in the vendored engine, P1 in any multi-token engine deployment or if the shared token leaks.
findings.recommendation: In runner.reject/runner.edit require who == requester_ref or who in approver_refs, matching get_proposal.

findings.title: Direct-adapter and model-provider API keys omitted from engine redaction list
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/assembly.py:293-305 (_secret_values lists 7 secrets, none of x_ads_*/openai_ads_api_key/model keys)
engine/src/paid_media_agent/runtime/profiles.py extra_secrets defaults () and is never set
findings.description: RedactionMiddleware scrubs tool results/exceptions by the explicit secrets list plus a fixed regex set. The X Ads consumer/access credentials and model-provider API keys are opaque strings absent from the explicit list; the generic regex only catches them adjacent to a key=/token= label, so a raw token echoed standalone in an upstream error body/stack can reach the model, Slack and logs unredacted. Static reachability, not an observed leak.
findings.recommendation: Drive redaction from the full SecretStr registry (populate extra_secrets) so new credentials scrub automatically; the value-based pass is the only reliable scrubber for opaque tokens.

findings.title: Provider-supplied readOnlyHint is the sole trust anchor for read/write classification
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/catalog.py:162-190 (classification reads annotations.get('readOnlyHint') straight from Pipeboard MCP metadata)
findings.description: A tool with readOnlyHint=true is admitted as a model-callable READ (with no proposal/approval/WriteGate) if it has an account arg and evades the mutate|raw|delete|remove|purge deny patterns. A hostile or buggy Pipeboard endpoint could mislabel a mutating tool (e.g. campaign_update) as read-only and the host would invoke it as a read, bypassing the entire write-governance stack. The deepest single trust assumption in the design; contingent on the trusted MCP backbone being compromised/incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Treat readOnlyHint as a hint, not authority; maintain an explicit host-side read-tool-name allowlist so a tool must be named to be callable; alarm when a catalog refresh flips a tool's class/hint.

findings.title: High/moderate transitive vulnerabilities reach the cloud app and MCP server
evidence: E9 pnpm audit --prod exit 1: sharp<0.35.4 (via next), fast-uri/ip-address/qs (via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk->express/ajv), hono<4.13.7 XSS; 6 high + 11 moderate
findings.description: The MCP SDK pulls a vulnerable Express/ajv/hono chain into production and next pulls a vulnerable sharp. Carried from E9's executed audit.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade the MCP SDK and Next.js to versions whose transitive graph clears audit, or add pnpm.overrides to force patched fast-uri/qs/ip-address/hono/sharp. Pair with SEC-05/SEC-13.

findings.title: MCP refresh-token rotation has no reuse detection/family revocation and revocation does not cascade
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/mcp-oauth-repository.ts:239-255 (consumed refresh token accepted within 60s grace, merely rejected after - no family revocation)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/mcp-oauth-repository.ts:300-317 (revoking access token updates only access table; revoking refresh updates only refresh table)
findings.description: RFC 9700 4.14.2 reuse-detection/family-revocation and RFC 7009 2.1 revocation cascade are unmet. A stolen refresh token redeemed before the legitimate client rotates yields a fresh valid pair; revoking one token leaves the sibling live for up to its lifetime.
findings.recommendation: On presentation of a consumed refresh token outside the grace window, revoke all refresh+access tokens for that (client_id,user_id,resource) and log a security event; cascade access-token revocation when a refresh token is revoked.

findings.title: Engine reasons over synthetic fixtures in both demo and live mode while adport applies results to real accounts (deferred headline)
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:383-388 (live mode forced to sample via model_copy)
README.md:116-118 (presents live mode as real accounts)
findings.description: The host hard-pins the engine's read side to bundled sample fixtures in both modes. In live mode a real model answers performance questions and generates budget/status proposals from synthetic campaigns, and the bridge can translate those onto real accounts via alias rows. From a security lens this is a GAP plus a latent financial-risk design flaw (real money moved on analysis of data that is not the tenant's), not an exploitable defect today (no live deployment; adport preview still shows the real current value). It does not change any of the 15 safety invariants. This is the biggest docs-vs-code contradiction and why SEC-01 is 'latent P0 the day real data flows'. I defer the product/architecture headline to the architecture/AI council seats as a P1 blocker.
findings.recommendation: Design a real per-tenant live data path (per-tenant engine instance or an adport-side read bridge feeding the tenant's normalized data) before offering live mode; add a boot assertion refusing MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=false unless the engine /health reports a non-sample data mode; block alias bindings to non-sandbox providers while the engine is sample-pinned.

contradictions: Engine reports IDOR severity: E4/E10 rated P2-today-latent-P0 vs E1/E5/J2/J3/J5 P1. RESOLVED to P1 (latent P0) against code - the defect is the un-scoped production route (reports/engine/route.ts:16-24, [name]/route.ts:10-31), the demo sample-pin is an incidental mitigant; J2's in-process probe had caller B download caller A's report (VERIFIED_RUNTIME), settling the cross-tenant path is real. E4/E10 were over-anchored to the demo pin. Winner: J / E1 / E5 / E11.

Self-approval / four-eyes: E10-06 rated the null-created_by skip P3 vs J2-03 three-vector P2. RESOLVED to P2 against code - I re-read all three vectors and confirmed the control is absent entirely on the API-key/MCP apply path (PolicyEngine checks provider+hash only, no actor; apiPrincipal has no userId - app/api/v1/tools/[tool]/route.ts:5-13, engine.ts:104) and off by default in the demo template (.env.example:49). E10-06 under-counted the surface. Winner: J2.

J2-08 'demo mode mixes synthetic and real paths' vs invariant 14 'demo cannot affect production accounts'. NOT a true contradiction: invariant 14 (no demo write reaches a real ad platform) HOLDS - sandbox provider is credential-free and PolicyEngine.apply rejects a provider-mismatched pending (engine.ts:104). J2-08's valid point is operational hygiene (process-wide flag interleaves sandbox and real audit/pending rows); carried as a separate P2 hygiene finding. Both correct about different things.

'Cloud master secrets injected into engine container' present in J2-04 (P2) but absent from the entire E-series. No conflict - a real blast-radius gap the E-series missed (docker-compose.yml:17,40,47 both services share env_file: .env). Adopted as SEC-29 P2. Winner: J2.

Reports-route line numbers differ (E11 cites :17-20; J2 cites :35-43). The behavior is identical and verified in the current file (GET at 16-24, no org scope); stale citation in one report, not a factual disagreement. No severity impact.

UNRESOLVED - SEC-04 P1 vs P0: turns on whether Next.js image-optimization/next/og is reachable from any route. Neither E9 nor K4 traced route reachability. E9 side: 'escalates to P0 if reachable'; no agent proved reachability. Open - NOT_VERIFIED.

UNRESOLVED - SEC-01 P1 vs P0: turns on production topology (multi-org on one engine + a real-data report host wired to the unscoped routes). Not decidable from the repo; docker-compose shows a single engine consistent with the risk but not proof of multi-org production use. Open - NOT_VERIFIED.
not_verified: No runtime exploitation by K4 (no live Postgres/Supabase/Stripe in sandbox): SEC-02 concurrent double-apply, SEC-03 out-of-order Stripe, SEC-24 dedup TOCTOU are VERIFIED_CODE not VERIFIED_RUNTIME; the reports cross-tenant read is VERIFIED_RUNTIME only via J2's in-process probe.
SEC-04 / SEC-12 carry E9's VERIFIED_RUNTIME pnpm audit (no network to re-run); Next.js image-optimization/next/og route reachability not traced (SEC-04 P1 vs P0 open).
Invariant 10 currency/budget units verified only for google/meta/tiktok/snapchat; apple/microsoft/reddit/spotify/pinterest/linkedin/x NOT_VERIFIED in depth.
Runtime Supabase cookie SameSite value (affects SEC-16 CSRF/consent-CSRF severity).
Runtime DB login identity vs adport_backend and whether the postgres.js role GUC is applied at runtime (affects SEC-18 RLS backstop).
Whether the hosting GitHub repo adds a root .github not present in this checkout (affects SEC-05 non-execution, INFERRED).
MCP mcp-oauth.database.test.ts and other DB-integration/concurrency tests not executed (no DB).
SEC-09 engine reject/edit horizontal-authz not exercised against a multi-token engine (mitigated in-product, so left VERIFIED_CODE).
K4.summary: Re-adjudicated all six P1 security findings (SEC-01 reports IDOR, SEC-02 non-atomic apply/replay, SEC-03 Stripe ordering, SEC-04 Next.js RCE, SEC-05 no root CI, SEC-06 MCP grant lifecycle) by re-reading the cited code myself; all six HELD at P1 and no present-day P0 survives (the reports IDOR is bounded to synthetic data today by the engine sample-pin, so P1/latent-P0). Produced the authoritative 15-invariant table independently: 9 HOLD, 5 PARTIAL, 1 BROKEN (replay, invariant 12). 24 spot-checks: 22 HELD, 2 PARTIAL (self-approval env default diverges across two templates), 0 FAILED. Resolved the two real E-vs-J disagreements against code: reports IDOR severity P1 (J/E1/E5 over E4/E10's P2-today) and the four-eyes self-approval control upgraded P3->P2 (J2-03's three-vector finding over E10-06). Added two findings the E-series missed from the J red team: cloud master secrets injected into the engine container (SEC-29, P2) and unauthenticated engine /docs+/markting/info (SEC-30, P3). The strongest property - the single human-gated write path (invariants 1,2,3,8,14) - is real and defended in depth; the headline risks are the BROKEN replay invariant, the un-isolated reports surface, un-re-checked budget caps at apply, and the live-mode-over-fixtures design flaw (deferred to the architecture seat as a P1 product blocker). Two P1-vs-P0 questions (SEC-01, SEC-04) remain open on deployment/runtime facts not decidable from the repo.

findings.title: Partial-conversion ratios emit an authoritative CPA/ROAS that can be ~3.5x wrong
findings.description: Within one entity/window spend is summed over every row but conversions only over rows that reported them, so CPA = full_spend / partial_conversions. B1 probe: 7x$100 with 10 conv on 2 days -> CPA 70 vs true 20. The per-entity/per-platform ratio is NOT suppressed (only the cross-platform total is).
findings.recommendation: Emit a ratio only when numerator and denominator cover the same row/day set; else None with a partial-basis label. Resolves B1-02(P2) vs A13-10(P3) -> P2 for the per-entity ratio.

findings.title: Partial impressions/clicks silently undercount totals and distort CTR/CPM/CVR
findings.description: A gapped impressions/clicks day sets no flag; aggregate returns a reduced denominator and derived CTR/CPM/CVR are wrong while missing=(). The window is not suppressed because suppression never inspects impressions/clicks gaps.
findings.recommendation: Extend the missing-metric guard to all four additive metrics; require per-metric day-coverage == window day-count before emitting a ratio.

findings.title: 'reconciled' is tautological on live data and the report stamps reconciled:true regardless
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/compute.py:225-248 (provider checks gated on totals keys live reads never carry)
findings.description: The only unconditional reconciliation check compares two quantities derived from the same rows; provider control totals exist only in fixtures. The report emits headline reconciled:true even when a per-platform reconciliation in the body failed.
findings.recommendation: Tri-state reconciliation requiring an external oracle (covering conversions/value, not just spend); pass comparison.reconciled into report_summary.

findings.title: Cross-platform blended CPA/ROAS mixes incompatible attribution and reaches the rendered report; the attribution flag is dead
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/reports/render.py:166-172 (caveat only a footnote, only when >1 platform)
findings.description: Blended portfolio CPA/ROAS sums Meta 7d-click/1d-view purchases with Google click-based conversions (and Apple installs / Pinterest checkouts via K5-05). Model structured view is spend-only, but the human PDF/HTML report shows the blended figure with only a footnote caveat and no machine guard.
findings.recommendation: Populate an Attribution descriptor per row; set ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS and suppress blended conversions/CPA/ROAS when signatures differ. Resolves A12-04(P3) vs A13-01/B2-02(P2) -> P2.

findings.title: Conversion-definition conflation within and across platforms
findings.description: One field 'conversions' holds purchases for some platforms, any configured action for Google/TikTok, installs for Apple. Summing them and deriving a portfolio CPA/ROAS compares non-comparable events; the 'results' key can promote a non-purchase optimisation event into the purchase column. Nothing records which event each count is.
findings.recommendation: Carry conversion_event/conversion_source_key per row; refuse or segment cross-platform aggregation across differing event kinds; drop 'results' from the purchase key list.

findings.title: Conversion-lag / incompleteness protection is fixture-only; live trailing days are treated as settled
findings.description: The wiki tells the model 'last N days' ends at data_complete_through, but no live path ever sets it, so yesterday's still-maturing conversions are treated as final. Period deltas understate the current window vs a matured previous window.
findings.recommendation: Derive data_complete_through on the host (provider-reported, else today - per-platform lag); treat an unknown boundary as immature, never complete.

findings.title: No statistical significance / sample-sufficiency engine; small-base noise emitted as a structured signal
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/summary.py:27,118-125 (relative-only day flag, no floor; 2->3 conversions flagged conversions_moved_up)
findings.description: The only analysis is arithmetic deltas; a 100% swing on a base of 1 looks identical to a real trend, and the structured flags/flagged_days the model consumes carry noise as if it were signal. Sample size never gates anything.
findings.recommendation: Attach the base (conversions/clicks) to every rate delta; compute a crude CI / small-base floor so the output distinguishes signal from noise.

findings.title: Proposals carry no evidence linkage and blank-able plans; risk classification is blind to data basis
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/write_tools.py:30-44 (reason required; measurement_plan/reversal_plan default ''; no analysis_artifact_id, no sample size, no window)
findings.description: A proposal cannot be traced to the data that justified it; a budget cut backed by 36 conversions and one backed by 3,600 produce identical risk surfaces; the measurement plan can be empty for a budget/status flip. This is the single most important enabler of 'recommend on insufficient data'. Backstops are unenforced prose + the human approval gate (real but not a data-sufficiency check), hence P2 not P1.
findings.recommendation: Require a cited analysis-artifact id, non-empty measurement + rollback plans for budget/status ops, and surface sample size + trust tier on the approval card.

findings.title: Merchant-facing overview ROAS tile is structurally 0x and sums across currencies/providers
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/live-data.tsx:33-41 (reduces every row; value += conversion_value ?? 0 -> 0; roas = value/spend -> 0; no currency grouping)
findings.description: The first profitability number an Arabic-first merchant sees is wrong by construction (0x) while the per-campaign table shows real per-row ROAS; headline Spend/Conversions tiles sum USD+SAR and double-count purchases. summarizeReport already groups by currency and reconstructs ROAS and is not used. Violates reporting-semantics.md:15. Static verification; Next.js not run.
findings.recommendation: Request conversion_value (or reuse summarizeReport), render one tile group per currency, label tiles platform-attributed, add a test asserting a non-zero tile for sandbox data.

findings.title: Zero-/three-decimal currency produces a 100x/10x budget write; declared unit ignored
evidence: platform/packages/meta/src/provider.ts:20 (CENTS_TO_MICROS = 10_000) applied at :333,334,452,522,523,568,614 with no currency check
findings.description: Bridge and Meta provider assume 2-decimal currency. A JPY 30,000 budget is written as 3,000,000; the percentage-delta cap compares micros-to-micros so it is blind. Latent: reachable only on the live-write path (demo/fixtures USD); requires a non-2-decimal account + an approved write. Kept at P1 (serious financial risk) with reachability flagged; not P0 because not exploited today.
findings.recommendation: Per-currency minor-unit offsets (2/0/3 decimal); validate after.unit against an enum; add JPY/KWD fixtures and an end-to-end bridge test.

findings.title: Budget percentage cap bypassed when prior budget unknown; default policy has no absolute ceiling

K5.summary: The engine's arithmetic over the data it is handed is trustworthy (Decimal, None-safe, never-average-ratios, intra-read currency hard-error, test-covered), but the provenance and trust machinery around it is fixture-shaped: on the live path every gate meant to say 'this number is not settled/reconciled/comparable yet' is off, tautological, or prose-only, so live data enters at trust tier T1 and is rendered with T3/T4 confidence. I re-verified 12 load-bearing citations first-hand and all held, including the DA-01 mitigation nuance (model summary is spend-only but the full blended scorecard reaches the human report with only a footnote caveat). Headline data-trust defects I vouch for at P2: partial-conversion and partial-impression ratios emitted as authoritative (can be ~3.5x wrong), a tautological/hardcoded 'reconciled' signal, a cross-platform CPA/ROAS blending incompatible attribution with a dead ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS flag, conversion-definition conflation, fixture-only conversion-lag protection, no significance/sample-sufficiency engine (2->3-conversion noise emitted as a signal), proposals with no evidence linkage, a structurally-0x merchant ROAS tile that sums currencies, divergent dual measurement engines, and a bypassable budget cap. One P1 (latent): a 100x budget write for zero-decimal currencies on the live-write path. Sample sufficiency is wholly absent and no surfaced number may legitimately carry a computed confidence today. I resolved the two real severity disagreements (attribution blend and partial-conversion CPA) to P2 and kept the zero-decimal budget at P1-latent. I defined a 9-rule minimum data-trust floor (explicit gating trust tier, earned reconciliation, maturity gate, ratio integrity, sample-sufficiency floor, attribution-compatibility gate, evidence linkage on proposals, currency/unit integrity, synthetic isolation) that must be enforced in code before any recommendation may carry a confidence score.

No CI runs any audited command. The only executed tenant-isolation/concurrency evidence (D5's two Postgres runs, J2's probe) is out of band and not in CI. Verdict: green is not ready — do not treat tests pass as safe to run real ad spend until the concurrency and route-authorization suites are added, CI runs them (DB + cross-stack lanes), the P1 is fixed, and a live-mode canary exists. Confidence 0.86.

findings.title: Master encryption key has no KMS/escrow and no working rotation

findings.description: Credential confidentiality rests on one symmetric env-var key. A DB restore without the exact key renders every provider_credentials.ciphertext permanently undecryptable; rotating the key in place destroys all ciphertext (self-inflicted data loss). The key_version column exists but is never used for key selection.
findings.recommendation: KMS-held key with a key id embedded in each ciphertext envelope, a decrypt-only keyring, and a bulk re-encrypt job; version the API-key pepper the same way; document that DR restore needs the matching key version.

The report-index cross-tenant exposure is rated P1/latent-P0 by the security seat (E11) on the un-isolated /reports route - consistent with this operability framing.
findings.recommendation: Move the report index to Postgres keyed by org (drop global 50-cap); back the kill switch with shared DB/config state checked on every write; remove the in-process report lock in favour of DB concurrency before scaling.

findings.title: Cloud pool max:10 with direct (non-pooler) DB URL unsafe on serverless; no statement/idle timeouts

findings.title: Webhook idempotency not atomic with effect; no ordering/recency guard; no dunning

K8.summary: markting-ai is NOT ready for a first paying customer, and the repo's own docs/TODO.md:18-22 and deployment-model.md:49-58 say so. The shipped artifact is a local, proposal-only demo (writes disabled, sample data, plain HTTP, Supabase outside compose); the production topology the blocker list is about does not exist in the repo and could not be built or run in this sandbox. I vouch for 9 P1 blockers before a paying customer: B1 no backup/restore, B2 encryption key with no KMS/escrow and broken rotation, B3 no usage metering of the dominant AI cost, B4 cannot contract under own name (upstream branding), B5 only destructive supabase db reset as a migration path, B6 no TLS edge, B7 no root CI so the tenant-isolation DB suite never runs, B8 no graceful shutdown/drain, and B9 non-cluster-safe shared state (global report-index file + per-process kill switch) - B8/B9 conditional on operating as a real service / scaling / live writes. 11 P2 should-haves follow (unaudited money-spending apply, no metrics/alerting/tracing, unstructured logs, liveness-as-readiness health, markting_* retention gap, serverless pool risk, webhook ordering/dunning, process-wide report lock, no image-build/root secret scan). I ran 15 spot-checks, all HELD (0 FAILED). I resolved four cross-agent tensions - most importantly that the pnpm-runnability split between F1 and H2 is sandbox/corepack state (not a code fact) and that F1's 19 engine-test failures are a stale KILL_SWITCH residue, not a code defect. The authoritative NOT_VERIFIED ledger (Docker builds, live stack, live Stripe/OAuth/model, real Supabase, restore drill) is itself a production gate: these are known unknowns a networked CI runner and a staging environment must close before launch. None of the P1s is a hidden defect; all are acknowledged or structurally obvious - to the project's credit - but each gates money and tenant ad-budgets. Memo at docs/audit/agents/K8.md.
